provenance: kawa commit ea99698 (docs/research/gear-fish-matrix.json); ROM tests gear-start-rom.test.ts, fight-chain-rom.test.ts, fish-size-bite-rom.test.ts
title: Which gear helps which fish, and by how much (the fight start at the hook)
basis: Thai ROM tables (bank 05 pointer table 05:8000) and the hook routine 04:8C96, read in Ghidra and proven by ROM tests in apps/web/src/shared/native-macros (gear-start-rom.test.ts, fight-chain-rom.test.ts, fish-size-bite-rom.test.ts). gear-start-rom.test.ts also rebuilds every field and number of this file from the ROM and fails if one differs.

notch.meaning: The fight starts with the mask $11FE = 2^n - 1 (0, 1, 3, 7, 15, 31, 63); n is the notch, 0 easiest, 6 hardest. The meter climbs one notch per pull tick and at 63 the fish surges and is lost (fight-chain-rom.test.ts). One notch lower = one more tick before the loss. 'mistakes allowed' in the wiki is 6 - n.

bands.measure: $1EB1, the hooked fish's own size (the stock cell's size word, in cm), copied at 04:8717 from 7F:1E8A + cell*2
bands.arrays: Per-band arrays are [<=15, 16..35, >35]; null = this fish never has a size in that band.

size.rule: A new fish gets size floor(min/2) + random mod floor(min/2), i.e. floor(min/2) .. 2*floor(min/2)-1 (03:83B0..83C5); each later stocking pass that picks its cell adds 1 (03:83CB..83DF); past the record max the cell is emptied. So a fish's size runs from floor(min/2) to max, not min to max. min = fish record +0, max = +1.
size.evidence: 03:83A6..85C5 (same code for all six areas, $085A = 7..12), fish-size-bite-rom.test.ts

order: 2. float/sinker method ($0C14 0/1): bait +1 or hook +1 equal to the fish id -> easier once (they do not stack), else the hook selector (+0) by size (04:8D4B..8D99, 8DC0..8E32)
2. lure method ($0C14 2): lure +2 equal to the fish id -> easier, else the lure selector (+1) by size (04:8D9C..8DB2)
2. fly method ($0C14 3): the fly BODY selector (+6) by size; no fish-name field (04:8DB5..8DBD)
3. unless rod +4 equals the fish id (04:8E35): rod class 0 pays 0/1/2 notches harder for <=15 / 16..35 / >35, class 1 pays 1/0/1, class 2 pays 2/1/0 (04:8E40..8EBE)

rod.fields: style +0 (1 float/ayu, 2 casting, 4 lure, 8 fly: which method the rod fishes), reach +3, match +4 (fish id the rod is named for), class +7, price +10
rod.effect: class step, then the size penalty unless named for the fish. reach x $150 = $1ED7 range line (04:871E..872E): a fish past it when the meter is full takes the tackle (04:9C4B..9C5C).

hook.effect: float/sinker only. Named for the fish: easier in every band. Else its selector by size.

bait.effect: float/sinker only. Named for the fish: easier once, replacing the hook selector (a named hook adds nothing more). Any other bait: no effect on the start; it only decides whether the fish bites.

float.effect: None on the fight start (the hook routine never reads $1250..$125E; gear-start-rom.test.ts writes other values and the start is unchanged). It picks the route: a sinker also needs fish record +13 bit 8 before the bait mask (04:E9AB route, wiki fish-acceptance-research.md).

lure.fields: selector +1 ($1228), match +2 ($122A), acceptance mask word +6 ($1232), price +8
lure.effect: Named for the fish: easier. Else its selector by size.
lure.evidence: gear-start-rom.test.ts (method word set to 2 at a float strike; the same routine runs)

fly.table: 05:800C -> 05:AA52, 11 bytes, 134 rows (64 ordinary bodies listed), loaded by 03:D0D9 from the body id $1238 (04:D491)
fly.fields: selector +6 ($1248), body +0/+2 pick the bait mask used at the bite (+2 != 0 -> bait 4, else +0 == 1 -> bait 8, else bait 7), price +9
fly.effect: Body selector by size. Wing and tail are not read by the hook routine.
fly.evidence: gear-start-rom.test.ts (method word set to 3); body-to-bait rule from the wiki (fish-acceptance-research.md, 04:D47C..D500, emulator-tested)

acceptance.rule: A fish bites only if (bait, lure or fly-bait mask word +6) & fish record word +15 != 0. Float also needs record +3 != 0, sinker also record +13 bit 8.
acceptance.evidence: Read in this ROM: float 04:E573..E579, sinker 04:EB0B..EB11 (after +13 bit 8 and the +3 random check), lure 04:EBFD..EC03, fly 04:E6C9..E6CF (also ANDs $1FA7). Float gate run in fish-size-bite-rom.test.ts; all four emulator-tested in the wiki (fish-acceptance-research.md, Japanese ROM, whose 72 fish rows equal this ROM's, see checks)
acceptance.notModelled: The fly's extra body/wing low-bit lock ($1FA7, 04:D4AF) and the lure route's $1348 & 8080 condition decide whether a given cast can bite, not which fish.

fields.fish[].record: raw record: min +0, max +1, baseMask +10, acceptMask word +15, biteThreshold +3, byte13 +13
fields.fish[].size: the sizes this fish really has (floor(min/2)..max) and the bands they cover
fields.fish[].baseNotch: notch of the record's base mask, before any gear
fields.fish[].accepts: item ids that pass the bite mask: bait (float route), baitSinker (sinker route), lure, fly (body ids)
fields.fish[].namedFor: items whose match field is this fish
fields.fish[].effect: per category, groups of items with the same own effect in notches per band (negative = easier). rod = class step + size penalty (0 if named); hook/lure/fly = selector or -1 if named; bait = -1 if named else 0. Clamping at 0 and 6 is not applied here.
fields.fish[].best[method]: method = bait (float and sinker rods), lure, fly. start = best start notch per band over every legal kit of accepted items; worst = worst; item[category] = groups of items by the best start each can still reach with the other slots chosen freely (clamped, in the game's order). null = the fish accepts nothing for that method.
fields.items: every item's raw fields used above, with names (ja from the ROM name table, th from the Thai patch, en from the research wiki)

unknowns: Which rod reach a fish needs: the range line is rod +3 x $150 and the fish's run is simulated only in the wiki's ported engine (gear-effects.md), not proven here.
Catch share per start notch: proven only that every notch lower moves the surge and the loss later in the same fight (fight-chain-rom.test.ts); the percentage depends on the player's rhythm.
Every 24 pull ticks the fight makes $11FE one notch harder (04:9C75..9C86); how often a rest resets the meter to $11FE (04:95BE, 04:9676, 04:9AD6) was not traced.
Lure and fly: the start rule was run by setting the method word at a float strike, not by a real lure or fly bite (the wiki's interpreter captures cover real lure and fly hooks).
Decoy ayu (bait 23, named for fish 56): its own fight is not traced; the start rule applies to it like any bait.
Names: fish ids align with the wiki's Japanese-ROM name table because all 72 rows (masks, thresholds) are equal; the Thai ROM's own name text was not decoded.
